This article analyzes **Indikator 14: Andelen af nydiagnosticerede patienter med atrieflimren, som får intrakraniel blødning inden for 1 år** (Indicator 14: The proportion of newly diagnosed patients with atrial fibrillation who suffer an intracranial hemorrhage within 1 year). The metric evaluates patient safety and treatment outcomes across different geographical levels in [[danmark|Danmark]], tracking how often patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] experience a severe bleeding complication, specifically an [[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]], within their first year of diagnosis.

In the 2021/22 period, the national average for [[danmark|Danmark]] was 0.7%, with 140 out of 21,045 patients experiencing this complication [^src1]. Among the regions, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] recorded the highest proportion at 0.8% (40 out of 5,069 patients) [^src1]. Conversely, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] tied for the lowest proportion, each reporting a rate of 0.6% [^src1]. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] fell in the middle at 0.7% [^src1]. 

The data includes a column for "Standard opfyldt" (Standard met), which uniformly displays "0 (0)" for all regions and the national level [^src1]. This indicates that either no specific numerical standard was set for this indicator, or the metric is tracked purely for observational purposes rather than against a strict target threshold.

Looking at the historical trend from 2019/20 to 2021/22, the national rate remained highly stable, fluctuating only slightly between 0.7% and 0.8% [^src1]. However, some regions showed slight improvements (reductions in hemorrhage rates). [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] decreased from 0.8% in both 2019/20 and 2020/21 down to 0.6% in 2021/22 [^src1]. Similarly, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] dropped from 0.8% in 2019/20 and 0.9% in 2020/21 to 0.6% in 2021/22 [^src1]. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] remained relatively flat, hovering between 0.6% and 0.7% across the three periods [^src1]. There are no significant outliers in this dataset; the variation between the highest and lowest regional rates is a mere 0.2 percentage points, demonstrating a consistently low and uniform incidence of this severe complication across the country.

**Broader Report Context**
While this analysis focuses on the specific data for Indicator 14 found on page 99 of the 2023 report [^src1], the complete 2023 and 2024 reports contain extensive additional data, methodologies, and analyses across many other sections. The 2023 report includes foundational methodologies and introductions [^src4] [^src5], specific regional and clinical deep dives [^src6] [^src11] [^src12], broader contextual analyses surrounding this indicator [^src14], and further hospital-level evaluations [^src18] [^src20] [^src22]. Similarly, the 2024 report provides updated methodologies and introductory frameworks [^src2] [^src7] [^src23], comprehensive regional performance metrics [^src8] [^src9] [^src10], and extensive supplementary clinical evaluations [^src3] [^src13] [^src15] [^src16] [^src17] [^src19] [^src21] [^src24] [^src25].
